title: Including fibrant objects preserves coherent localization
statement:
Use ordinary nerves, quasicategories, equivalences and entire coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing all the categories below. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with terminal object $1$, and let $W,P$ be classes of arrows containing all isomorphisms and closed under composition. Suppose $W$ has two-out-of-three. Call $a$ fibrant when $a\to1$ belongs to $P$, and let $\mathcal A_f$ be the full subcategory of fibrant objects. Assume that for every $p:x\to y$ in $P$ with $x,y$ fibrant, and every $v:y'\to y$ with $y'$ fibrant, the pullback $x'=y'\times_yx$ exists, is fibrant, and $x'\to y'$ belongs to $P$; if $p\in W$, also $x'\to y'\in W$. Assume further that every $f:a\to b$ with fibrant codomain has a factorization $a\xrightarrow{w}a'\xrightarrow{p}b$ with $w\in W$, $p\in P$, and $a'$ fibrant. No functoriality of these factorizations is assumed, and arbitrary objects of $\mathcal A$ need not be fibrant.

Both ordinary nerves have coherent localizations at their specified weak equivalences, and the inclusion induces an equivalence
$$L(\mathcal A_f,W|_{\mathcal A_f})\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }L(\mathcal A,W).$$
Here a coherent localization $q:N\mathcal B\to L(\mathcal B,V)$ means that, for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$, restriction along $q$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(L(\mathcal B,V),\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal B,\mathcal E)$ on functors inverting $V$, retaining every coherent transformation and higher simplex.
